data.why: The app bundles two converged demo datasets (Mn3Ga neutron TOF Rietveld, GaTa4Se8 X-ray PDF) as TypeScript modules under src/examples/, loaded in-browser via demo buttons; no external files are needed as uploads. A third 'magnetic' AWO4 demo exists but is only offered when a dev-only git-ignored data/ folder is present, so it will not appear in this run.

goals: Load a bundled example and inspect the observed/calculated/difference Rietveld fit for a two-phase neutron TOF powder pattern
Refine nuclear structure parameters (lattice, atomic positions, occupancies, microstructure/profile terms) and read out refined values with esds
Solve a magnetic structure: search propagation vector k from magnetic peaks, enumerate magnetic subgroups (BNS/OG), and refine ordered moments
Refine a PDF/mPDF G(r) fit against X-ray pair distribution function data and compare refined cell parameters to a reference
Load one's own diffraction data (GSAS-II/GSAS/FullProf instrument files, SHELX or FullProf hkl lists, CIF/mCIF structures) and run the same refinement workflow on it
Assess fit quality and uncertainty (wR, R1, least-squares esds, Bayesian posterior via ensemble MCMC or NUTS) and compare against established tools (GSAS-II, FullProf, SHELXL, PDFfit2)

review.summary: The tree captures MATERIA's purpose well for its two demos: the Rietveld, magnetic-symmetry, uncertainty and PDF workflows are cut into sensible scientific tasks and lift-able features, and most cited screens support the claims. It needs fixes before filing: two mis-cited screens, a wrong esd in t20, a couple of UI-level tasks and an odd phase order, plus missing stages for loading your own data, single-crystal refinement, mPDF and the Copilot.
